stance.label: Taiwan bear-market bounce · DCA on plan

headline: Taiwan jumps 956 points back above 39,000 as PCB and substrates lead; foreigners sell 9th day, TSMC slips
summary: Local funds drove today's Taiwan rally while foreign investors kept selling stocks and futures; by the rules it is still a bear market with rising risk. Gains centered on PCB, substrates and cooling, while TSMC closed lower. US markets are shut for Thanksgiving tonight; next, watch whether the TAIEX can retake 39,858.

watch.note: Closed 39,151.81 on 11/26, about 1.8% below; retake it and hold the 200-day line 5 days to return to a pullback

watch.label: TAIEX 200-day line
watch.note: 6.0% below on 11/26; the line still rises (+2.59%); flattening would mean the long-term trend turns down

overview.lead: Taiwan rallied hard today, but local funds and small caps carried it; foreigners have not stopped selling, so the bear call stands.
points: The TAIEX rose 956 points to 39,152.
The OTC index gained 5.03%; small caps bounced harder than the main board.
Foreigners sold NT$49.2B, a 9th straight day of selling, while local funds kept buying.
TSMC (2330) fell 0.23%; the biggest weight did not join in.
US markets close for Thanksgiving tonight, so Taiwan gets no US lead tomorrow.

focus.lead: Yuanta Taiwan 50 led the nine today, but the two Taiwan funds' NAVs only run to 11/25 and miss today's bounce.
points: Yuanta Taiwan 50 (0050) rose 2.82%, −20.3% from its peak.
Unimicron (3037), Elite Material (2383) and AVC (3017), shared by Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8), all surged today.
The two Taiwan funds' 11/25 NAVs fell 5.25% and 4.3%; the next NAV may recover some.
QQQ is 4.1% from tier 4; one US holiday changes nothing.
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan (TW000T5011A9) NAV only runs to 11/24.

position.lead: No new trigger under the framework today; the rally pushed 0050 further from tier 5.
points: 0050 has used 70% of its reserve; tier 5 is 12.2% away.
QQQ has used 45% of its reserve; tier 4 is 4.1% away.
SPY has used 25% of its reserve; tier 3 is 7.6% away.
Fidelity Japan Value (LU0997587083) is 8.5% from tier 5 (11/25 NAV).
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan is 11.2% from tier 5 (11/24 NAV).
AB Select US Equity (LU0683600562) is 8.0% from tier 3 (11/25 NAV).
Allianz Taiwan Technology, Cathay Taiwan High Dividend and AB International Technology (LU0060230025) have used every tier.

macro.lead: No new US data today; rate-hike expectations still weigh on richly valued stocks, and credit markets are calm.
points: Core PCE rose 3.3% y/y (released 11/25); a December hike is close to certain.
The 10-year Treasury yield was 4.85% (11/25).
High-yield spreads were 3.72% (11/24), far from the 5% alarm line.
USD/TWD was 32.921 (11/25); the Taiwan dollar is weak but not plunging.

sentiment.lead: Taiwan sentiment is recovering from panic, but breadth is still at the bottom; the bounce has not spread.
points: Only 14% of Taiwan stocks are above the 200-day line; the breadth-collapse light stays on.
Only 7% are above the 50-day line, a deep washout.
CNN Fear & Greed is 15.2, extreme fear in the US.
VIX was 28.29 (11/25); the US holiday leaves it unchanged.

sectors.lead: The electronics groups hit hardest over the past month staged a relief rally, led by PCB, substrates, cooling and networking.
points: Electronic components rose 8.31%, still down about 30% over a month.
Optoelectronics rose 6.81%, still down 29% over a month.
Unimicron hit limit-up and Elite Material rose 9.09%; substrates and PCB led.
Accton (2345) and AVC rose nearly 10%; networking and cooling followed.
TSMC closed lower and MediaTek (2454) rose only 1.65%; heavyweights lagged.

taiwan.lead: The bleeding in flows has not stopped: foreigners sold for a 9th day and added to futures shorts; local funds and retail held up the rally.
points: Foreigners sold NT$49.18B, about NT$470.8B over nine days.
Local investment trusts bought NT$23.05B, a 3rd straight day.
Foreign net short TAIEX futures rose 566 contracts to 106,275 contracts.
Margin loans were NT$434.1B (11/25), down about 30% in 20 days; deleveraging is deep.
Combined turnover was NT$943.6B; the bounce came on volume.

watch.lead: US markets are closed tonight; what decides Taiwan next is when foreigners stop selling, plus December's payrolls, FOMC and CPI.
points: 11/26 US Thanksgiving holiday; no economic data or earnings tonight.
11/27 US early close (Taipei 11/28 02:00); thin volume.
12/1 Jensen Huang faces a closed-door US House committee interview.
12/4 US November payrolls (Taipei 21:30).
12/10 FOMC decision before dawn Taipei time; November CPI that evening.

regime.lead: By the rules, Taiwan is still a bear market with rising risk; today's jump is not enough to change that. The US is still a pullback.
points: Trend: the TAIEX is 6.0% below its 200-day line for 9 days, but the line still rises.
Systemic lights: 2 on for Taiwan, the US below its 200-day line and Taiwan breadth collapse.
Credit, the economy and financial conditions are fine; high-yield spreads are 3.72%, far from 5%.
Capitulation signals: 2 on for Taiwan, margin deleveraging and a breadth washout; oversold and extreme foreign selling are off.
Taiwan has always gone past −20% from here: all 10 cases since 2000, and 4 passed −30%.
Only 3 cases were this fast and 1 passed −30%; the sample is too small, use it only as a reference.
What flips it: close back above 39,858, then hold the 200-day line 41,664 for five days, and it returns to a pullback.
3+ risk lights would make it a bear driven by the economy or credit.
